title: phegopteris rostrata
intro: Phegopteris rostrata, commonly known as the beech fern, is a species of fern in the family Dryopteridaceae. It is a type of vascular plant that belongs to the division Pteridophyta, and is native to the mountainous regions of Asia. Phegopteris rostrata has been traditionally used in medicine for its potential health benefits, which include reducing inflammation and improving cardiovascular health due to its antioxidant properties. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and polysaccharides, which exhibit therapeutic actions such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities.
